This document is an Air Intelligence Information Report (AIIR), a standardized U.S. Air Force reporting form used to record raw information of potential intelligence value for later analysis. The form served as a primary vehicle for U.S. Air Force field intelligence collection throughout the early Cold War, until defense-wide reporting standards were established in the early 1960s. This AIIR records a January 18, 1957, incident over Saudi Arabia in which the crew of a U.S. Air Force B-52 aircraft reported detecting an unidentified return on the aircraft’s gunnery scope for approximately five to seven minutes. The report characterizes the unidentified return as smaller than one produced by another B-52 operating in the area. All descriptive and estimative language contained in this report reflects the reporter’s subjective interpretation at the time of the event. Such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics.
この文書は、後の分析のために潜在的な諜報価値の生の情報を記録するために使用される標準化された米国空軍報告書である航空情報情報報告書 (AIIR) です。このフォームは、1960 年代初頭に国防全体の報告基準が確立されるまで、冷戦初期を通じて米空軍の現場情報収集の主要手段として機能しました。この AIIR は、1957 年 1 月 18 日、サウジアラビア上空で、米空軍 B-52 航空機の乗組員が約 5 ～ 7 分間、同機の砲撃照準器で正体不明の帰還を検知したと報告した事件を記録している。報告書は、未確認の帰還は、その地域で活動している別のB-52によって生成されたものよりも小さいと特徴付けています。このレポートに含まれるすべての説明的および推定的な表現は、イベント発生時の記者の主観的な解釈を反映しています。このような特徴付けは、オブジェクト固有の機能やパフォーマンス特性の有無を決定的に示すものとして解釈されるべきではありません。

B-52（機体番号394）がCastle AFB発、Strategic Air Command任務（作戦名は原文不鮮明）に参加中、A-3A砲術レーダー（ガンナリースコープ）で未確認航空機を補足したとの報告。接触時の記録は“27 north - 47 00.St (approximately)”、B-52の対地速度842ノット、航高度39,000フィート、夜間で接触継続時間は約5～7分。未確認機の反応はスコープの約6000ヤードマーカー付近にあり、B-52が左にバンクした際にスコープ左側へ消失（Baghdad Flight Identification Region方向へ消えたように見えたと記載）。未確認反応は同時に記録された別のB-52の反応（5000ヤードマーカー）より小さかった。文書は機密指定（SECRET）で、スコープ上の物体は予期された航空機ではないと評価されている。
During a Strategic Air Command mission (operation name illegible in the document), B-52 aircraft number 394 from Castle AFB detected an unidentified aircraft on an A-3A gunnery scope. The report records contact at “27 north - 47 00.St (approximately)”; the B-52’s ground speed was 842 knots and altitude 39,000 feet at night; contact lasted about 5–7 minutes. The unidentified return remained near the 6,000-yard marker on the scope and disappeared to the left when the B-52 banked left (noted as disappearing toward the Baghdad Flight Identification Region). The unidentified return was smaller than a simultaneous return from another B-52 at the 5,000-yard marker. The document is classified SECRET and assesses the contact as not being an expected aircraft.

This document is an administrative, programmatic, or contractor-produced record related to the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP), a Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA)-administered program active from 2008 to 2012. AAWSAP’s official scope of work identified 12 technical research areas relating to potential aerospace threats over a time horizon of more than 40 years. As part of the broader program record, the file documents how AAWSAP was scoped, organized, tasked, funded, executed, or described at a particular point in time. This April 2010 Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) investigation report documents field deployments to a Utah property and surrounding communities during March and April 2010. The report states that BAASS personnel interviewed local residents, law enforcement officers, ranchers, business owners, and tribal community members about reported anomalous events; used handheld sensors to collect environmental measurements; planned plant-based biosensor experiments; and sought photographic, acoustic, and chemical evidence of purported anomalous phenomena. It also records extensive reported accounts involving “dog-like bipedal creatures,” orbs of light, “little people,” “prehistoric-looking” birds, among other phenomena, and states that BAASS intended to use interactive methods to attempt communication with the presumed source of reported anomalous activity.
この文書は、2008 年から 2012 年まで活動していた国防情報局 (DIA) 管理のプログラムである先進航空宇宙兵器システム応用プログラム (AAWSAP) に関連する、管理的、プログラム的、または請負業者によって作成された記録です。AAWSAP の公式作業範囲では、40 年以上の期間にわたる潜在的な航空宇宙の脅威に関連する 12 の技術研究分野が特定されています。より広範なプログラム記録の一部として、このファイルには、特定の時点で AAWSAP の範囲がどのように設定され、組織され、任務が与えられ、資金提供され、実行され、または説明されたのかが文書化されています。この 2010 年 4 月の Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) 調査報告書には、2010 年 3 月から 4 月にかけてユタ州の敷地と周辺地域社会への現場展開が記録されています。報告書には、BAASS 職員が報告された異常な出来事について地元住民、法執行官、牧場主、経営者、部族コミュニティのメンバーにインタビューしたと記載されています。ハンドヘルドセンサーを使用して環境測定値を収集しました。計画されている植物ベースのバイオセンサー実験。そして異常現象とされる写真、音響、化学的証拠を求めた。また、「犬のような二足歩行の生き物」、光の球体、「小人」、「先史時代のような」鳥などの現象に関する広範な報告が記録されており、BAASSは報告された異常活動の発生源と推定されるものとのコミュニケーションを試みるために対話型の方法を使用するつもりだったと述べられている。

2010年3月22–26日および4月19–23日に、AAP Person 7（タスクフォース主任）を含むBAASSのチーム（捜査官2名、科学者2名）がユタ州フォートダチェスネの牧場周辺で調査を実施した。目的は未確認生物や光の目撃の証拠収集（聞き取り、デジタルゲームカメラ設置、ポータブルセンサー測定、土壌化学・電磁・放射線の基線取得、植物を用いたバイオセンサー実験）である。7台のMoultrieデジタルゲームカメラが牧場と関係者の敷地に設置され、メモリカードは週次で保全されるプロトコルが確立された。これまでに25名超が面談を受け、11名が二足歩行の「犬/オオカミ様」生物を、4名が身長約3フィートの毛深い「トロール様」生物を目撃したと報告している。その他に大型「ミミズ様」、プテロダクティル様の鳥状個体、「小人」、近接の光球・UFO報告も複数ある。雪上の未同定の足跡写真や、有刺鉄線フェンスを“通り抜ける”ように見える足跡の写真、現場近傍から採取した毛髪サンプルが入手され、DNA分析が進行中である。目撃位置をプロットした地図では、目撃者の移動方向の直線延長の交点が牧場付近に3カ所あり、夜間監視候補地として示されている。現地での電磁観測では少なくとも1地点（Location 02）で前日には検出されなかった強い信号が水平・垂直偏波で検出され、スパイクはおおむね1210/1213/1216 MHzおよび1232.5/1235.5/1238.5 MHzにあり、帯域は約1164–1240 MHzであり、これら周波数帯は地球観測・航法等に割り当てられていると記述されている。調査記録には被面談者（匿名化された1843(a)(2)家族）の複数の詳細な遭遇記述（深夜の遠吠え、窓から差し入れられた約3フィートの毛覆いのある腕、6–9フィート程度の影や大きな黄色い目、“Basket Lady”と呼ばれる長毛の女の目撃、翼幅約12フィートの鳥状個体、透明に波打つ「ポータル」像、持続的なハミング音など）が含まれる。報告書は追加の測定と分析が必要であると結んでいる。
On March 22–26 and April 19–23, 2010, a BAASS team including AAP Person 7 (Task Force Director) conducted investigations at and around a Utah ranch near Fort Duchesne. The team (two investigators and two scientists) aimed to collect evidence of reported unidentified creatures and lights via interviews, deployment of seven Moultrie digital game cameras, portable sensor measurements (magnetic field, EM spectrum, ionizing radiation, soil chemistry), and plant-based biosensor experiments. A protocol was established for weekly securing of camera memory cards. More than 25 people were interviewed; 11 independent witnesses reported bipedal dog-/wolf-like creatures, 4 reported small (~3 ft) hairy “troll”-like creatures, and additional reports described large worm-like entities, pterodactyl-like birds, “little people,” and orbs/UF O-like lights. BAASS obtained photographs of unidentified tracks in snow (including tracks appearing to merge and pass through barbed wire) and collected multiple hair samples now undergoing DNA analysis. A sightings map created from witness-reported locations and bearings produced three convergence points near the ranch, suggested as priority night-watch sites. Electromagnetic sweeps found an anomalous strong signal at Location 02 not present the prior day; distinct spikes near 1210/1213/1216 MHz and 1232.5/1235.5/1238.5 MHz were reported, within an ~1164–1240 MHz band (frequencies allocated to earth observation, radionavigation, etc.); signals were detected on both horizontal and vertical polarizations and require further study. The investigative record includes detailed encounters from the anonymized 1843(a)(2) family: nighttime howling, shadows/figures ~6–9 ft tall, an approx. 3-ft arm covered in dark hair with claw-like fingers inserted through a window, large yellow reflective eyes, a long-haired “Basket Lady” sighting, a bird-like creature with ~12-ft wingspan, descriptions of a clear rippling “portal,” and intermittent humming; the report concludes additional measurements and analysis are needed.

DOW-UAP-D176, Triangular UAP AARO Memorandum for Record, 2026
DOW-UAP-D176、Triangular UAP AARO 記録用覚書、2026 年
Department of War
米国戦争省
10/23/26
2026年10月23日（Release 07）
June, 2026
Western United States
米国西部
PDF
PDF
This document is a memorandum for record documenting an AARO witness debrief concerning reported unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) observations at a sensitive national security site in the western United States over two days in 2026. AARO considers this incident to warrant further investigation due to the close alignment of the phenomena’s reported morphological features and kinematic profiles with those of other reported incidents in the western United States region. The memorandum records an interview with two Federal Special Agents and incorporates a corroborating account from a third official positioned at a separate observation post. The memorandum describes a primary event in which the reporting individuals stated that a triangular object rose vertically, remained stationary, and then banked and descended into a canyon. It records their descriptions of the object’s shape, color, apparent thermal signature, perceived lack of conventional propulsion features, and absence of an associated audible signature. The memorandum further records a secondary observation on the following evening, and a subsequent ground search that found no visible debris or evidence of an impact in the accessible survey area. The file is an investigative record preserving witness accounts, chronology, and associated analytic support material developed by the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) and does not present a conclusive finding regarding the nature or origin of the reported object or objects. All descriptive and estimative language reported by the individuals interviewed reflects their subjective interpretations at the time of the event. Such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics.
この文書は、2026年に米国西部の国家安全保障上の重要な現場で報告された未確認異常現象（UAP）観察に関するAARO目撃者の報告を文書化した記録用覚書である。AAROは、報告された現象の形態学的特徴および運動学的プロファイルが米国西部地域で報告された他の事件のそれと密接に一致しているため、この事件はさらなる調査が必要であると考えている。この覚書には2人の連邦特別捜査官とのインタビューが記録されており、別の監視所に配置されている3人目の当局者からの裏付けとなる説明が組み込まれている。この覚書には、三角形の物体が垂直に上昇し、静止した後、堤防に傾いて峡谷に落ちていったと報告者らが述べた主要な出来事が記載されている。これには、物体の形状、色、見かけの熱的特徴、従来の推進機能の欠如の認識、および関連する可聴特徴の欠如に関する説明が記録されます。覚書にはさらに、翌日の夕方の二次観測と、アクセス可能な調査エリアで目に見える破片や衝突の証拠が見つからなかったその後の地上調査も記録されている。このファイルは、全ドメイン異常解決局 (AARO) によって開発された目撃者の証言、年表、および関連する分析サポート資料を保存する調査記録であり、報告されたオブジェクトの性質や起源に関する決定的な結果を示すものではありません。インタビューされた個人によって報告されたすべての説明的および推定的な言葉は、出来事当時の主観的な解釈を反映しています。このような特徴付けは、オブジェクト固有の機能やパフォーマンス特性の有無を決定的に示すものとして解釈されるべきではありません。
初公開
documents.summaryText:
AAROの報告によれば、2026年の2023Lに観測員らが尾根上空でマットブラックの三角形状かつ極めて低アスペクト比の未確認機体を記録した。推定寸法は翼幅13–15ft、胴体長6–9ft、垂直厚1–2ft、観測距離は観測点西方約1.4–3.2マイル。機体は約10秒かけて200–300ftまで完全に垂直に上昇し、その後約20秒間安定ホバリングしたのち、加速ランプや段階的ピッチ変化を伴わずに2–3秒で高速度の水平飛行へ移行し峡谷へ地形に沿って降下して視認を失った。全過程で可聴音はなく、赤外線では機体全体が均一な熱シグネチャを示し、排気や局所的高温源は観測されなかった。外装は継ぎ目や開口、制御面、風防等の識別可能な構造を欠いていた。目撃者に生理的影響や機器上の異常は報告されず、翌朝の地上調査でも残骸や地面損傷は見つかっていない。報告は出来事当時の報告者の解釈を反映するもので、対象の固有特性の有無を決定付けるものではない。
Per the AARO report, in 2026 at 2023L observers documented an unidentified matte-black, low-aspect-ratio triangular craft over a ridge. Estimated dimensions: 13–15 ft wingspan, 6–9 ft fuselage length, 1–2 ft vertical thickness; range roughly 1.4–3.2 miles west of the primary observation post. The craft executed a controlled vertical ascent (~10 s) to ~200–300 ft, held a stable hover (~20 s), then transitioned without observable acceleration ramp into high-speed horizontal flight, performing a banking, terrain-hugging descent into a canyon in ~2–3 s before disappearing. It produced no detectable acoustic signature throughout; IR imagery showed a spatially uniform thermal signature with no localized hot spots, exhaust, or propulsion signatures. The exterior appeared continuous and featureless with no discernible openings, control surfaces, or cockpit features. Witnesses reported no physiological effects or equipment anomalies; a ground survey the next morning found no wreckage or ground/vegetation damage. The report notes these are the reporter’s interpretations at the time and do not conclusively establish intrinsic object characteristics.

This file contains an Air Intelligence Information Report (AIIR), a standardized U.S. Air Force reporting form used to record raw information of potential intelligence value for later analysis. The form served as a primary vehicle for U.S. Air Force field intelligence collection throughout the early Cold War, until defense-wide reporting standards were established in the early 1960s. This AIIR records a June 25, 1952, incident over Catalina Island, California, in which three Boy Scouts attending a summer camp at Camp Fox reported observing silver “flying saucers” moving at an estimated speed faster than that of a conventional jet. The report also describes the object as climbing quickly before apparently disintegrating. A comment by the preparing officer indicated that no attempt was made to establish the reliability of the report and characterized the experience of the observers as “probably meager at best.” All descriptive and estimative language contained in this report reflects the reporter’s subjective interpretation at the time of the event. Such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics.

At 1610Z on 31 December 1956 an F-86D (serial 52-9995), flown by 1st Lt. Ted Brunson over the Guam radio range holding pattern, reported a blinking white light. The report states that unless the launched lighted balloon malfunctioned and remained at relatively low altitude, the unidentified flying object cannot be readily explained. Report prepared by Capt. Alan G. Pound (Air Technical Intelligence Liaison Officer).

He reported that it moved from east to west at very high speed, intermittently disappearing and reappearing while leaving behind a narrow luminous trail or ribbon. Siasが夜空に緑青色で真珠のように輝く球状物を観察したとする報告（地元紙掲載記事を基にした陳述）。球は満月よりやや小さく、右側に金属状の筋があり、東–西方向に非常に速く移動、断続的に消現して光の帯（球径の約1/7）を残しながら3–5秒間で地平線へ消えた。寮の孤児と約3km離れた場所の管理人も同時刻に観察を報告している。Siasは観測角度を南方45°（天頂と地平線の間）とし、バチカン天文台長Father Junkesの座標計算では、地球影の外への出現点までの距離を南方約1681kmまたは南西約1091kmと推定、見かけ直径0.5°を当てはめると実直径は約14.7kmまたは約9.3kmになり得ると算出された。Junkesは色・輝度を鉄・ニッケル含有の天体によるものとする一方、Siasは人為的飛行体としては寸法が大きすぎると結論づけ、超自然的または他国起因の可能性も示唆した。作成担当官はSiasを知的で熱心だが強い個性（ほぼ熱狂的）と評し、Siasは観測記録の所有権を米大使館に譲渡する意向を表明している。添付に教授のスケッチあり。
On 27 August 1952 at about 21:45 in Sassari, Sardinia, Prof. G. B. Sias reported observing a bright, green-blue, mother-of-pearl luminous sphere in the night sky. The object, slightly smaller than the full moon with metallic streaks on its right side, moved rapidly east–west, intermittently disappearing and reappearing while leaving a narrow luminous ribbon about one-seventh the sphere's diameter; the sighting lasted roughly 3–5 seconds. Two other witnesses (an orphan and a caretaker ~3 km away) corroborated observation. Sias placed the sighting at about 45° south between zenith and horizon; Father Junkes (Vatican Observatory director) calculated, using solar position, that the emergence point from Earth's shadow would lie roughly 1681 km south or 1091 km southwest, which—if the apparent diameter were 0.5°—implies an actual diameter on the order of ~14.7 km or ~9.3 km. Junkes suggested the colors/luminosity could be due to iron-nickel content of a celestial body and judged a conventional terrestrial 'flying saucer' unlikely because of the implied size. The reporting officer described Sias as intelligent and earnest but intense; Sias stated he would transfer the record/ownership to the U.S. Embassy. A sketch by Sias was enclosed.

Source: extracts from Tempelhof air traffic control logs dated 11 August 1953. On 10 August 1953 at 1936Z a British European Airways DC-3 (callsign recorded as GALJI/GA.GIP) en route via the Center Corridor reported observing red rocket-like objects being fired about one nautical mile ahead. At 2245Z the BEA pilot reported a stationary red light about 20 nautical miles west of Genthin (coords 5224B/1209E) at approximately 5,000 ft (not above 5,500 ft). At 2315Z the Soviets checked the reported red light but could not account for it. An Air Intelligence report (5004th Air Intel Sv Sq, IR 5004-40-53) documents that Raleigh Iyapanna, a 14-year-old Eskimo from Little Diomede Island, reported seeing a light on the southern tip of Big Diomede Island (USSR). The report text notes the report was made on 6 October 1953 and evaluated on 8 October 1953. The sighting time is given approximately as 0810Z (the document contains both 081015Z and 081025Z). The light lasted several seconds, was observed at an estimated height of about 95 feet above sea level, and was described as about the size of a nickel at arm's length with a color like a burning match or a dim flashlight; the source thought it came from a large flashlight or spotlight. The source had been watching Big Diomede nightly for the prior week and was judged fairly reliable by the reporting officer. Weather was clear, stars visible, Big Diomede outlined against the sky, wind from the north ≈5 mph. The preparer noted the location is unusual for human presence and difficult to reach at night; while signaling to the Alaskan mainland from the southern tip is possible, there is no evidence the light served that purpose.

This document is an Air Intelligence Information Report (AIIR), a standardized U.S. Air Force reporting form used to record raw information of potential intelligence value for later analysis. The form served as a primary vehicle for U.S. Air Force field intelligence collection throughout the early Cold War, until defense-wide reporting standards were established in the early 1960s. This AIIR records a December 17, 1953, incident near Hässleholm, Sweden, translated from a local media report. At 1437 hours, Transair chief pilot Captain Ulf Christiernsson and crew chief Olle Johansson reported observing an object approaching their DC-3 from the opposite direction, approximately 600 meters (1,969 feet) below their aircraft, which was flying at about 2,150 meters (7,054 feet). The aircrew described a “shining metal spherical elliptical object” and estimated its speed as approximately the speed of sound. Christiernsson described the object as strongly metallic, nearly round, and slightly elliptical. He reported that it remained visible for six to seven seconds, produced no visible exhaust or condensation trail, and initially appeared to him to be a jet or possibly an unmanned “robot.” The Swedish Defense Staff reportedly identified no Swedish aircraft in the area at that time and stated that it would examine possible radar observations. The report also includes a brief character sketch of Christiernsson based on the account of a personal contact, who characterized him as “most untrustworthy,” and notes that Swedish authorities had begun an investigation into the incident. All descriptive and estimative language contained in this report reflects the reporter’s subjective interpretation at the time of the event. Such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics. AARO Comment: Based on the reported aircraft altitude and relative separation, the object’s reported altitude was approximately 1,550 meters (5,085 feet). Under standard atmospheric conditions, the speed of sound at that altitude is approximately 748 mph.

This document is a Flying Objects Report prepared in accordance with Air Force Regulation 200-2, which established guidance for reporting unidentified flying objects. The report records an incident near Seymour, Indiana, in which two civilian reporters stated that they observed two airborne objects while traveling by car. The report does not identify an exact event date; its weather assessment addresses conditions during the period December 8–15, 1953. The report describes the incident as consisting of a “brilliant moving light” and two large, white, cloudy or gaseous objects in a staggered formation. It further describes four bright points of light within each object and a bluish-white, vapor-like trail. The report describes the object kinematics as an in-line approach with a steady descent, a stationary interval of unreported duration, and a rapid departure along an abrupt upward angle toward the southwest. It records an estimated direct observation period of three to four minutes, with a total elapsed period of five to six minutes that included changes in the vehicle’s route. All descriptive and estimative language contained in this report reflects the reporter’s subjective interpretation at the time of the event. Such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics.

This November 2008 MUFON report for BAASS contains two main studies: one on "Lift" and one on power generation (cold fusion). The Lift study defines lift distinct from conventional propulsion and reviews three conventional lift mechanisms (buoyancy, aerodynamic lift, and propeller/VTOL). It notes many low‑noise hovering UFO reports that are not readily explained by air displacement and examines using the Earth's magnetic field via superconducting toroidal magnetic dipoles (force F = M·gradB, torque M×B), including gyroscopic stabilization, expected motion signatures, and reported compass disturbances. The report also considers electrostatic levitation using the Earth's electric field (requiring high‑voltage charge injection and producing local ionization/glow) and the possibility of combining magnetic and electrostatic methods. It recommends investment in superconductor and nanotechnology research as the highest‑payoff path toward gravity‑control experiments, proposes a small‑scale superconducting toroid demonstration with a specified team and a 26‑week milestone schedule, and includes Appendix A with quantitative design relations (field gradients, latitude dependence, and required ampere‑meter^2 and current density orders). Ducted‑fan VTOL is discussed but investment is not currently recommended. Project CAPELLA is a proposal (Report No.001, Dec 10, 2008, IAAP Person 5 / Documatica Research) to develop a data warehouse to support research on unusual aerial phenomena (UAP) and related anomalies. The report includes an overview plus three appendices: A) classification methodology and reliability indicators, B) modeling of information categories including high-strangeness elements, and C) data structures and software platforms. It reviews historical efforts (Battelle/Project Blue Book, Condon, UFOCAT/CUFOS, Magonia, MUFON, GEiPAN, etc.) and notes that many disparate catalogs (30+ active) suffer from lack of standards and data validation. Requirements: support a family of catalogs, rapid deployment, global data coverage, enable advanced analysis and data mining, dynamic data validation, and allow researchers to test hypotheses. The authors recommend a data-warehouse approach (standard structure and coding over existing files) implemented rapidly with off-the-shelf software (EXCEL suggested for initial flat-file work) and a small specialist team to avoid prior projects' pitfalls. Data acquisition priorities include converting existing catalogs (e.g., NIDS), collecting new raw data, conducting a literature review, and linking external experts. Integration of foreign/private catalogs should address legal/IP issues and visibility policies; outreach to European researchers is planned. Staffing: initial roles are database administrator, data analyst, and quality-control coordinator; in year two add a statistician and a literature-focused data analyst. Estimated costs: about $610,000 in year one and $830,000 in year two. Appendix A outlines principles for an observation-behavior-based classification system and reliability measures.

The report repeatedly notes the proprietary/confidential status of the information.

本資料は2009年4月のBigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) 月次進捗報告の抜粋である。主な内容は以下の通り。採用：4月1–30日に281件の履歴書を受領、初期スクリーニング実施。面接を継続し、Bigelow Aerospaceからの移籍を含めて2009年4月30日時点で常勤35名・非常勤6名と管理者を配置。今後2–3か月で初年度目標の約50–60名を採用する見込みだが、米国内全域をカバーするには追加資金が必要とされる。セキュリティ・クリアランス：複数の主要職員（管理者、副管理者、シニアアナリスト、リード等）および請負業者がワシントンD.C.で手続きを完了し、他2名が調査開始段階にある。Earthtech契約：2008年12月にEarthTechへ24–30本のポジションペーパー作成契約を付与。これらは以前の12分野（揚力、推進、制御、発電、時空移動、材料、構造、署名低減、ヒューマンインターフェース、人体影響、兵装、周辺分野）を拡張したもので、全体納品は2009年7月予定。寄稿者は大学・企業・コンサルタント等多数で、反重力、真空エネルギー、ワープドライブ、MEMSバイオセンサー、IEC融合、ワームホール、先進材料、メタマテリアル、レーザー／パルスパワー兵器、重力波通信、FTL/エンタングル通信、核宇宙推進等のテーマ別レポートが5–6月に順次予定されている。MUFON契約：2009年2月にMUFONとの購入契約を締結し、米国内の重要なUAP報告の数時間以内の通知、調査報告、写真や試料など物的証拠の受領権を取得。BAASSは解析用の複数ラボを有し、ラスベガスに情報・法執行経験を持つ10名の迅速展開調査チームを配置しているが、国内全域をカバーするには人員が不足するとの記載。MUFON側のSIPプロジェクト報告では、2–3月に人員・ロジスティクス整備、Dispatch運用と現地展開準備を実施し、4月1日に運用開始。プロジェクト用に専用口座を設置し、CMSに「Category」「Dispatch Notes」フィールドを追加、Shiftboard/Skype/Gmail等を利用してDispatch Operatorsが自宅から勤務する仕組みを導入。Dispatchは太平洋時間6:00–22:00をカバーする4時間シフト制で、新着ケースはCMSで監視され、証人確認・分類後、重要（Cat 2/3）かつ最近の事案は州コーディネータと連携して派遣判断がなされ、BAASSへ通報される。報告はMUFONの生産性低下（特に4月の事例減少）に対するBAASSの懸念で締められている。

MUFON contract — In February 2009 BAASS executed a purchase order with MUFON to receive near‑real‑time notifications of significant UAP reports, investigator reports, and physical evidence (photos, digital recordings, soil/biological samples) for forensic analysis. MUFON uses Shiftboard, Skype and Gmail to enable Dispatch Operators (four‑hour shifts covering 6:00 AM–10:00 PM Pacific Time) to work virtually; DOs monitor MUFONCMS, contact witnesses, categorize cases, and escalate recent/Category 2–3 cases to State Coordinators for possible deployment, notifying BAASS when appropriate. This document is an excerpt of the Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) June 2009 monthly report (June 1–30, 2009). Recruitment: BAASS received 461 resumes, performed initial screening, conducted dozens of interviews, and as of June 30 employed 45 full‑time and 6 part‑time staff plus an administrator, including senior investigators (law enforcement/AFOSI backgrounds), engineers, scientists, support staff and security. Facilities: planning/design of a 5,000 sq.ft. underground vault at the Bigelow North Las Vegas site (3‑ft thick walls, concrete access tunnel, >15–20 ft of earth cover) targeted for late 2009/early 2010; purchase in escrow of five office buildings including a 5,000 sq.ft. lab, secure evidence storage and a SCIF, with occupancy planned by end of 2009. EarthTech contract: BAASS contracted EarthTech to produce 24–30 position papers on advanced aerospace vehicle physics (topics such as lift, propulsion, control, power, spacetime/temporal translation, materials, signature reduction, human interface/effects, armament); about 24 papers had been delivered by end of June, final delivery scheduled July 2009. MUFON contract: BAASS purchased rights to rapid notification of significant UAP reports, investigator reports and physical evidence; BAASS has labs and rapid‑response investigators but limited geographic coverage. MUFON’s reported spending and case volumes were below allocated amounts, prompting BAASS to propose reducing monthly payments for July–Oct 2009 (proposed $25,500/month) and to use unused prior allocations to supplement operations, with reevaluation in October 2009. MUFON acknowledged progress, accepted temporary reductions, and requested reassessment in October. The report also includes MUFON investigative case summaries (e.g., Scammon, Kansas, April 4, 2009: witness sketches/photos, object hovering ~200 ft, orange light, silent).

This document is an administrative, programmatic, or contractor-produced record related to the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP), a Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA)-administered program active from 2008 to 2012. AAWSAP’s official scope of work identified 12 technical research areas relating to potential aerospace threats over a time horizon of more than 40 years. This November 2009 Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) progress report summarizes contractor activities for the period November 1–30, 2009. The report focuses on AAWSAP investigative activity based on information received via the Mutual UFO Network (MUFON), progress on investigations centering on a ranch in Utah, and a preliminary report on a “blue orb” incident. It also records BAASS’s continued emphasis on field investigation, case database expansion, and focused inquiry into events at the Utah ranch and surrounding area, including creation of a separate database for those incidents.

This document is an administrative, programmatic, or contractor-produced record related to the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP), a Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA)-administered program active from 2008 to 2012. AAWSAP’s official scope of work identified 12 technical research areas relating to potential aerospace threats over a time horizon of more than 40 years. This November 2010 Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) contractor-authored capability statement presents BAASS’s analysis as technically rigorous and strategically valuable. The document appears intended not only to describe BAASS’s analytical capabilities but also to reinforce the case for the organization’s continued relevance and for the continuation of AAWSAP. The document summarizes the company’s self-assessment of the suitability of its personnel, software, equipment, field sensor, and data warehousing capabilities for analyzing unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP) and unidentified submerged objects (USOs). It includes excerpted case findings and uses selected case studies and modeling exercises as demonstrations of BAASS’s analytical capabilities. The report describes BAASS as combining field collection resources, historical databases, and computational tools such as ANSYS Multiphysics to model UAP incidents through engineering and physics analysis, including work on radar cross section, fluid behavior, acoustics, and aerodynamic performance. It also presents BAASS’s in-house capabilities as supporting both threat assessment and the study of advanced aerospace technologies, while asserting that analysis of UAP performance characteristics could inform future developments in propulsion, stealth, detection, and weapons systems.

This file contains the final personnel record of U.S. Air Force officer Howard M. McCoy, who left service as a Colonel, a senior field-grade officer responsible for significant operational and administrative duties. From December 1946 to August 1949, Colonel McCoy served as Deputy Commanding General for Intelligence (T-2), and later as Chief of the Intelligence Department, Headquarters, Air Materiel Command, at what is now known as Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. During his tenure, the Air Force initiated two significant studies centering on unidentified anomalous phenomena: Project SIGN and Project GRUDGE. He was among the senior Air Force intelligence officers involved in the early design, administration, and execution of those programs.

EOP-UAP-D002、外国物品回収のための省庁間調整に関する覚書、1963 年 5 月
Executive Office of the President
大統領行政府
10/23/26

5/29/63
Washington, D.C.
ワシントンD.C.
PDF
PDF
This document is an internal National Aeronautics and Space Council (NASC) memorandum from staff member R.W. Hale to Executive Secretary Edward C. Welsh. NASC was a 1958–1973 body within the Executive Office of the President responsible at the time for coordinating U.S. space policy. The memorandum records a May 28, 1963, meeting with Arnold Frutkin, Director of International Programs at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), concerning the development of a coordinated interagency policy for recovering reentering U.S. and Soviet space debris and satellite fragments that might land on foreign soil. This memorandum is associated with a larger body of interagency correspondence included in this collection under the title “USG-UAP-D002.” The memorandum highlights an interagency policy debate over organizational jurisdiction during the early Space Race. It states that the Department of State and Department of War sought to leverage NASA’s standing as a civilian scientific agency to help facilitate discreet recovery of sensitive space hardware while publicly returning non-sensitive components to the country of origin. As described in the memorandum, the proposed arrangement would have served several purposes: enabling access to adversary technologies, protecting U.S. technologies, preserving diplomatic goodwill, and obscuring the intelligence gathering dimension of technology recovery operations. The memorandum also presents Director Frutkin’s reaction to the proposed arrangement as “very negative.”
この文書は、職員 R.W. ヘイルから事務局長エドワード C. ウェルシュへの米国航空宇宙評議会 (NASC) の内部覚書です。 NASC は 1958 年から 1973 年にかけて、当時米国の宇宙政策の調整を担当する大統領府内の組織でした。この覚書には、1963年5月28日、米国航空宇宙局（NASA）の国際プログラム部長アーノルド・フルトキンとの会談の内容が記録されており、再突入する米ソのスペースデブリや外国の土壌に落下する可能性のある衛星の破片を回収するための省庁間連携政策の策定に関する内容が盛り込まれている。この覚書は、「USG-UAP-D002」というタイトルでこのコレクションに含まれる、より大きな機関間通信に関連付けられています。この覚書は、初期の宇宙開発競争における組織の管轄権をめぐる政府機関間の政策論争に焦点を当てている。同報告書によれば、国務省と陸軍省は、民間科学機関としての NASA の立場を利用して、機密性の高い宇宙用ハードウェアの慎重な回収を促進する一方で、非機密性の高いコンポーネントを原産国に公に返却することを支援しようとしたと述べられています。覚書に記載されているように、提案された取り決めは、敵の技術へのアクセスを可能にすること、米国の技術を保護すること、外交上の友好関係を維持すること、技術回収作戦の情報収集の側面を曖昧にすることなど、いくつかの目的を果たすはずだった。覚書ではまた、提案された取り決めに対するフルトキン長官の反応が「非常に否定的」であると述べている。
判定不能

USG-UAP-D002, Interagency Correspondence Concerning Space Fragments, 1962-1964
USG-UAP-D002、宇宙断片に関する省庁間通信、1962～1964 年
U.S. Government
米国政府
10/23/26
2026年10月23日（Release 07）
1962-1964
Washington, D.C.
ワシントンD.C.
PDF
PDF
This file contains a series of memoranda and correspondence exchanged among senior Executive Branch officials between October 2, 1962, and May 26, 1964, concerning the development of a policy framework and communications strategy for the recovery, handling, analysis, and disposition of materials associated with U.S. and foreign activities in space. Over the course of multiple drafts and revisions spanning nearly two years, the file documents efforts to establish jurisdictional boundaries based on the suspected origin and character of recovered material. In general, the proposed framework contemplated that material associated with a U.S. Department of Defense mission or equipment would be received, analyzed, and disposed of by the Department; that foreign space material would be turned over to the Department of Defense or the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), depending on the circumstances; and that the Department of State would coordinate with foreign governments to secure access to such material when recovered abroad. The correspondence also reflects efforts to assign responsibility for hazardous or radioactive materials to the Atomic Energy Commission. Various drafts alternated between assigning responsibility for handling materials whose origin could not be readily determined to the Department of Defense or to NASA. The correspondence also reflects concern with public perception regarding recovery activity and includes draft public statements describing the proposed framework. This public messaging included language designating NASA as the holding authority for foreign materials, while private correspondence described a parallel plan to exploit such materials for technical analysis. Ultimately, although these negotiations did not produce a settled policy framework, the correspondence illustrates interagency deliberations between senior officials in the context of the Space Race and the broader Cold War between the United States and the Soviet Union.
このファイルには、1962 年 10 月 2 日から 1964 年 5 月 26 日までの間に行政府の上級職員の間で交換された一連の覚書と通信が含まれており、宇宙における米国および外国の活動に関連する物質の回収、取り扱い、分析、処分のための政策枠組みとコミュニケーション戦略の開発に関して書かれています。このファイルには、ほぼ 2 年間にわたる複数の草案と修正を経て、回収された物質の疑わしい起源と性質に基づいて管轄境界を確立する取り組みが文書化されています。一般に、提案された枠組みでは、米国国防総省の任務または装備に関連する資料が国防総省によって受け取られ、分析され、廃棄されることが想定されていました。外国の宇宙物質は、状況に応じて国防総省またはアメリカ航空宇宙局（NASA）に引き渡されることになる。そして国務省は外国で回収された場合にはそのような資料へのアクセスを確保するために外国政府と調整するとした。この対応には、危険物質または放射性物質に対する責任を原子力委員会に割り当てる取り組みも反映されている。さまざまな草案では、起源がすぐに特定できない物質の取り扱い責任を国防総省または NASA に割り当てることが交互に行われていました。この書簡には、復興活動に関する国民の認識に対する懸念も反映されており、提案された枠組みを説明する公式声明の草案も含まれている。この公開メッセージには、NASA を外国資料の保管当局として指定する文言が含まれていましたが、私的な通信には、そのような資料を技術分析に活用する並行計画が記載されていました。最終的に、これらの交渉では政策枠組みはまとまらなかったものの、この書簡は、宇宙開発競争と米ソ間の広範な冷戦を背景とした政府高官間の政府機関間の協議を示している。

文書群は「Space Vehicle Fragments - Responsibilities and Procedures」を扱う国立安全保障ファイル（Charles E. Johnson宛、Box 018）に属する1962–1964年の草案・メモ・ルーティングスリップ等を含む。内容は宇宙機破片の受領・分析・処分に関する省庁間ガイドライン案と、対外回答用の公報文案である。主な点は、NASAを米国内に落下または取得された破片の指定責任機関とすること、ただしDODが自機打ち上げ品の受領・識別を単独で担うこと、外国外製破片は迅速にDODに引き渡して分析し最終的にNASAが管理して返還等を手配すること、AECは放射性・特殊核物質に関与する分析で参加すること、国務省は対外処分と外国領土での回収支援に関与することなどである。Julian Scheer（広報担当副管理者）による照会対応文例も含まれ、破片による被害の確率は極めて低く、SA-5やGT-1などで焼却を助ける設計措置を取っている旨の説明と、分析完了後に速やかに公表する旨が示されている。文書には会合（1963年11月6日、11月21日）やE.C. Welshの1963年11月15日付メモの記録があり、機密表示および1964年4月8日付の非機密化注記、制限コード(A,B,C)が付されている。
The papers, from the National Security File (Files of Charles E. Johnson, Box 018), are 1962–1964 drafts, memos and routing slips concerning interagency responsibility and procedures for handling space vehicle fragments. They set out draft guidelines designating NASA as the primary agency to receive, analyze and identify fragments falling into U.S. possession, with DOD retaining sole responsibility for fragments from DOD-launched vehicles. Foreign-origin fragments are to be expedited to DOD for analysis and then held by NASA pending return or other disposition; AEC participates for radioactive or special nuclear materials; State provides policy guidance and assistance for recovery in foreign territory; the Smithsonian and contractors may assist collection and analysis. Included are public-affairs guidance (Julian Scheer) advising minimal information in responses, statements that fragment impact risk is remote, examples of mitigation measures (e.g., SA-5 ballast, GT-1 heat‑shield modifications), and a pledge to publicize results after analysis. Records note meetings (Nov 6 and Nov 21, 1963), a Nov 15, 1963 memorandum from E.C. Welsh, classification markings and a declassification note (Apr 8, 1964), and restriction codes (A, B, C).
